blocks.x: How IoT, Twin & Robotics lands in Semiconductors & Hardware — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

Hardware companies run the longest R&D loops under the sharpest IP threats: design simulation, fab yield (their own or partners'), supply-chain visibility and product security. Compute acceleration and governed data are the compounding assets.

items: Multi-tier supply opaque; allocation shocks disrupt.

items: Your product becomes a service: device fleets, OTA and telemetry products with revenue attached.
Facilities that run themselves: BMS/IoT fusion, energy optimization and city-scale platforms.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: energy and utilization telemetry for sites (operating cost down measurably). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
